macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rise after weak jobs report
items.summary: The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq advanced after September payroll growth of 29,000 came in well below expectations, while unemployment rose to 4.2%. The Nasdaq reached a record high intraday as lower Treasury yields supported technology shares.

items.title: Markets cut expectations for October Fed rate hike
items.summary: Interest-rate traders sharply reduced bets on a Federal Reserve hike later this month following the weaker employment data. Pricing indicated roughly a 16% to 24% probability of a quarter-point hike, compared with substantially higher odds the previous week.

items.title: Euro-area inflation accelerates
items.summary: Eurozone consumer-price inflation rose to 3.8% year over year in September, above expectations, potentially complicating the European Central Bank’s policy outlook.

items.title: Tesla deliveries beat estimates
items.summary: Tesla reported third-quarter deliveries of 486,532 vehicles, exceeding analyst expectations, although deliveries declined sequentially and fell about 2% from a year earlier. The company also said it began volume production of the Tesla Semi while delaying the Roadster launch.

items.title: Nike shares fall on weak outlook and restructuring plans
items.summary: Nike dropped after reporting weaker-than-expected quarterly revenue and warning that its sales downturn could worsen during the fiscal year. The company also announced further job reductions and a reorganization of global business divisions.

items.title: Micron results support chip and AI stocks
items.summary: Micron’s upbeat quarterly results and guidance helped lift semiconductor and AI-infrastructure shares, contributing to Nasdaq outperformance and stronger Nasdaq-100 futures.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin reclaims $85,000 as crypto market rises
items.summary: Bitcoin rose about 2% over 24 hours to roughly $85,421, while the total cryptocurrency market capitalization increased 1% to approximately $2.99 trillion. Ethereum gained 1.1%, Solana 1.6%, and XRP 0.9%.[1]

items.title: SEC proposes easing crypto custody rules
items.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission proposed allowing investment advisers to custody clients’ crypto assets themselves when eligible custodians are unavailable, and permitting state trust companies to serve as crypto custodians.[5]

items.title: New York and Wyoming coordinate digital-asset oversight
items.summary: The two states agreed to cooperate on licensing reviews, examinations, and enforcement involving cryptocurrency companies operating across their jurisdictions.[5]

items.title: EU regulators scrutinize Binance MiCA exemption
items.summary: European regulators are reportedly examining Binance’s reliance on the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation’s reverse-solicitation exemption to serve some customers in the European Union without full authorization.[5]

items.title: IMF approves El Salvador disbursement despite bitcoin-related waiver
items.summary: The International Monetary Fund approved a $139 million disbursement to El Salvador after granting a waiver tied to the government’s breach of bitcoin accumulation limits.[1]

items.title: NEAR Intents identifies suspected $3.8 million exploiter
items.summary: NEAR Intents said it identified the individual linked to an exploit involving roughly $3.8 million and gave the person 48 hours to return the funds under a responsible-disclosure process.[1]

items.title: Blast plans to shut down Layer 2 network
items.summary: Blast announced plans to close its Layer 2 network and said users can withdraw funds through its standard interface until October 26, 2026.[8]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: 007 First Light update adds major features as sales surpass four million
items.summary: IO Interactive released the free Extended Operations update for 007 First Light, adding New Game Plus, a 00 difficulty mode, five TacSim missions and Photo Mode. The game has reportedly surpassed four million sales.

items.title: Critical Role joins ROCKBEASTS as co-publisher
items.summary: Critical Role announced a publishing partnership with LICHTHUND for ROCKBEASTS, a story-driven band-management RPG about guiding a 1990s grunge band from garage performances to stadium success. The game is planned for release in 2027.

items.title: Gaia Crisis revealed for PC
items.summary: InvertMouse, creator of Clea, announced Gaia Crisis, an anime-style action-horror game featuring puzzles, traps, enemies and more than 30 voice performers across 24 chapters.

items.title: End of Abyss launches on PC and consoles
items.summary: Section 9 Interactive and Epic Games Publishing released the top-down atmospheric horror game End of Abyss for PC and consoles.

items.title: Gray Zone Warfare announces Rogue Ops update
items.summary: Madfinger Games unveiled Rogue Ops, a major update for the open-world tactical shooter Gray Zone Warfare focused on player-versus-environment content.

items.title: Com2uS launches Hive Axyl backend platform
items.summary: Com2uS announced Hive Axyl, a game-development backend platform designed to help developers integrate backend services using natural-language requests.

items.title: Fortnitemares 2026 shop dates announced
items.summary: Epic Games revealed upcoming Fortnitemares 2026 shop dates, including collaborations and content featuring Black Clover, Freddy Krueger and Hollow Knight.

items.title: Diablo collection coming to Dead by Daylight
items.summary: Behaviour Interactive announced a Diablo-themed collection for Dead by Daylight, scheduled to arrive on October 20 as part of the game's Halloween-season content.
